answer: Throttle the birth rate of identities globally: admission difficulty rises with the recent rate of new joins and decays slowly, like an orchard that can only be planted so fast before the soil must rest. One honest agent joining alone meets low difficulty and enters quickly. A farm minting a thousand heads in a burst drives the shared difficulty up against all of them, so each later head pays a steeper toll and the whole planting stretches across real time. A lone yarrow seeds cheaply; a farm cannot populate its island of clones overnight.
